gap: No result ChatGPT got states that EcoFlow's US store sells its MC4-to-XT60i solar cable only in 2.5 m (8.2 ft). The 3.5 m (11.48 ft) cable is the plain XT60 version, which EcoFlow says works best with the older RIVER, RIVER Max/Pro/Plus, DELTA mini, DELTA and DELTA Max (1600). ChatGPT's '$24.99 EcoFlow MC4 to XT60i | 3.5m' card mixes up the two versions.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited pages. yourpowersetup.com only says EcoFlow 'distinguishes XT60i from XT60' and gives no lengths, models or amp ratings. stormwatts.com/solar-panel-compatibility gives port limits for DELTA 3 Plus, DELTA Pro 3 and Jackery, but not which EcoFlow cable version or length fits which generation. Neither gives the per-model cable lists from BLUETTI's store. The Jackery DC8020 extension adapter rules were in results 10 and 11 (faq.jackery.com, not cited), so that part is not new.
decides: It changes the EcoFlow cell of the answer. Owners of a RIVER 2 or later, DELTA 2, DELTA Max (2000) or DELTA Pro should pick the 2.5 m XT60i version. If they need more reach, they should add EcoFlow's 3 m MC4 extension pair ($29.99) rather than buy the '3.5 m XT60i' that ChatGPT's card implies. For BLUETTI, the store sells the 20 A MC4-to-XT60 lead ($29, on Dealectric's list) separately from the MC4-to-DC7909 lead ($19.90), which BLUETTI says is for the B80 or EB3A. Buyers have to match the lead to the station's port, not to the brand. For Jackery, original Explorer 240/300/500/1000 owners need a DC8020-to-DC7909 adapter, and E100 Plus, E240 V2 and E300 Plus owners need a DC8020-to-USB-C adapter, even with Jackery's own extension cable.
